texts.li: [summer] A trader's boy brought the news with a basket of eggs, not knowing what he carried: {TALE} is dead, months ago, and buried a long way from here. {A_nameDef} paid for the eggs, carried them to the kitchen, and has been standing in the yard since with nothing in {A_possessive} hands.

[worn] It came on the worst possible week. {A_nameDef}, already worn thin, heard from a traveler at the gate that {TALE} has died, far away and some time ago. {A_nameDef} said "oh" and nothing else, and went on with the work as if {A_pronoun} hadn't heard.

lines.li: [winter] They sat close to the fire with the shutters closed, and {A_nameDef} told the old stories in the order they happened, and then out of order when someone asked for one again.
{A_nameDef} walked out past the last field and sat where the land falls away, and came back at dusk with burrs on {A_possessive} trousers, and ate supper with the others.
[winter] The ground was hard, and {A_nameDef} dug the hole anyway. The young tree stands bare beside the fields with a stone at its foot, waiting for the spring.
{A_nameDef} took the hardest jobs going and didn't stop to talk. When the work ran out, {A_nameDef} found more.

texts.li: [winter] By the stove, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} spread a trader's blanket out to dry and set out the goods on it to sell. Among them is {TALE}. {A_nameDef} sat down hard when {A_pronoun} saw it: it was {A_possessive}, a long time ago.\n\n{X_nameDef} wants {COUNT} silver, and has noticed the sitting down.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} counts the silver and hands {TALE} over as if it were nothing much. {A_nameDef} holds it as if it were everything.
{B_nameDef} picks {TALE} up, finds a scratch, finds another, and keeps finding them until {X_nameDef} gives in at half the price. {A_nameDef} has it back, scratches and all.

riskLines.li: {B_nameDef} pushed once too often. {X_nameDef} put {TALE} back in the pack, tied it shut, and wouldn't open it again before leaving.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} hears {A_nameDef} out, looks at {TALE} a long while, and hands it across without taking anything. "Bought it off a thief, then," {X_nameDef} says. {FACTION} will hear the colony's side of it, and {X_nameDef}'s.

riskLines.li: {X_nameDef} calls it a lie to {A_nameDef}'s face and packs up on the spot. {TALE} leaves for {PLACE} in the bottom of the bag.

lines.li: {A_nameDef} puts it back on the blanket where it was, straightens it, and walks away. {X_nameDef} sells it before the day is out.

texts.li: [summer] The letter reached {A_nameDef} in the middle of the summer's work, carried by a trader who had it in his hat. Come home: there's {TALE}, and nobody else to see to it.\n\n{A_nameDef} hasn't put the letter down since, and has asked the council to decide.

[children] {A_nameDef} read the letter from home twice, then went and found the colony's children and watched them play for a long time. The people {A_pronoun} left want {A_objective} back for {TALE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} has asked the council to decide, because {A_pronoun} can't.

lines.li: The silver goes into a pouch sewn shut, with a letter folded round it, to go home with the next trader. It will pay for the hands {A_nameDef} can't be. {A_nameDef} wrote until the candle was out.
The colony walked {A_nameDef} to the gate. {A_nameDef} went with a full pack and a list of messages for people {A_pronoun} has never met, and didn't look back until the last bend.

texts.li: [winter] A cart has come through the snow with a load worth three times the {COUNT} silver its driver asks, and the driver, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, wants the sale done before dark. The tarp is stenciled with a storehouse mark from {PLACE}.\n\n{A_nameDef} has seen the mark before, on the carts that go past in the fall.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} counts the silver in the cart's shadow, unloads in a hurry and is off down the road. The goods go into the storeroom, and someone takes a knife to the marks on the sacks.

riskLines.li: {X_nameDef} took the silver and was gone. The goods hadn't been in the storeroom long before a rider from {PLACE} came asking about a stolen cart, and found them there with the marks half scraped. {FACTION} won't forget it.

lines.li: Word goes off to {PLACE}. {X_nameDef} sees which way the colony is looking at {X_objective}, pulls the sacking back over the load and goes, fast. {FACTION} send their thanks, and riders after the cart.
{X_nameDef} says the colony is passing up the bargain of the year, and drives the cart off to find someone less careful.

texts.li: [winter] Long nights are good for business, says {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, and taps the dice cup on the table. A game after supper for anyone who wants one, or a single game against the colony's best, {COUNT} silver a side.\n\n{A_nameDef}, the colony's sharpest head for numbers, is already watching {X_nameDef}'s hands.

[colony:Easygoing] The colony knows how to take an evening off, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has heard, and has come to help it lose some silver doing it. Games for anyone tonight, or one against {A_nameDef}, who looks clever, at {COUNT} silver a side.

lines.li: The games went on until the lamps needed filling. The colony came out ahead by the end, and {X_nameDef} paid up and asked to see the dice again, as if they might be the colony's fault.

riskLines.li: The table laughed all evening, and by the end most of the laughing was {X_nameDef}'s. The colony's purses are lighter for it.

lines.li: {A_nameDef} counted every throw and said nothing. On the last one {A_pronoun} took the pot, and {X_nameDef} sat back and laughed and paid.

riskLines.li: {A_nameDef} had {X_nameDef} worked out by the middle of the game, and lost anyway. {X_nameDef} pocketed the pot and said {A_nameDef} played better than most.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} took the colony's no with a bow and put the cup away, and was on the road again in the morning.

texts.li: [summer] A beast with {PLACE}'s brand on its flank walked in out of the heat yesterday, drank the trough dry and lay down in the colony's shade as if it had paid for it. {A_nameDef} has been feeding it.\n\n{FACTION} will be missing a good animal. They may not know where to look.

[river] The river brought it: a draft beast of {FACTION}'s, {PLACE}'s brand on its flank, washed down in the night and dragged out on the colony's bank, cold and furious. {A_nameDef} got it into the barn to dry off.\n\n{FACTION} will want it back, if they know where it went.

lines.li: A drover from {PLACE} came for the beast with a halter over one shoulder and a sack of something over the other, for the colony. The animal knew the drover and went without a fuss.
{FACTION}'s drover paid the fee coin by coin, looked the beast over for marks, and led it off without thanking anyone.
The brand is cut away and the hair let grow over it. The beast stays, and pulls for the colony as well as it ever did for {PLACE}.

riskLines.li: The brand was clipped, but not well enough. A trader of {FACTION}'s passing the pens stopped dead, looked at the animal and then at the colony, and went on without a word. {FACTION} know now.

texts.li: [spring] {X_nameDef} and two others of {FACTION} are walking to {PLACE} for the planting, and are early. They'd take a day's work here on the way: trees felled and trimmed for a meal each, or a winter's wood for {COUNT} silver.

[forest] Three of {FACTION}'s people came out of the trees with axes on their shoulders and asked who owns the woods. {X_nameDef} speaks for them: they'll fell and trim for a meal each, or cut the colony a winter's wood for {COUNT} silver, and be on their way to {PLACE} after.

lines.li: The three of them felled and trimmed until the light went, then ate their supper where they'd worked. The logs are lying out by the treeline where they fell.
{X_nameDef}'s crew went through the treeline like a storm and stopped only when they couldn't see the axe heads. The logs lie where they fell, enough to keep the stoves going a long while.
A hot meal went out to each of them. They ate it fast, thanked {A_nameDef} with their mouths full, and were off toward {PLACE}.
The three of them shouldered their axes and went on toward {PLACE} without arguing. Somebody up the road will have work.

texts.li: [summer] Summer is when {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} walks the settlements teaching, a day here and a day there. {A_nameDef} has already learned to spell {A_possessive} own name from {X_objective}, twice, for free.\n\nFor {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} would give the colony's children a proper day of it.

[colony:Learned] Word that the colony keeps books brought {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} out of {X_possessive} way to see them. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} first. For {COUNT} silver, {X_nameDef} will spend a day teaching the colony's children.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} kept the children at the table with slates until supper, and left each of them a sum to finish. {A_nameDef} finished {A_possessive} first and asked for another.
The grown-ups sat down after the children, and {X_nameDef} taught them exactly the same way. {A_nameDef} watched from the doorway, delighted, and corrected anyone who got one wrong.
{X_nameDef} left the children a long word each to spell, and was gone before they had them right.
{A_nameDef} and the two with {A_objective} went down the rows taking only the best, and argued over every plant. What came in before dark was the pick of the crop.
The colony leaves the fields to the frost and keeps to its work. {A_nameDef} has already said what they'll look like in the morning.

texts.li: [summer] The herd wouldn't settle last night, and in the morning {A_nameDef} found why: prints in the dust all round the pens, and a hole started under the fence where the ground is soft. It's {TALE}. It will be back tonight to finish the hole.

lines.li: The herd was brought in before dark and shut in behind the thick walls, complaining all the way.
The tracks came round once more in the night and then turned off toward the hills. Whatever it was has gone to find something easier.

riskLines.li: It came back and dug through where the fence was weakest. In the morning there was a hole under the gate, a long drag mark in the dirt, and one fewer animal in the pen.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} paid for every head of the herd, and the drovers kept them to the bank while they drank. The colony watched from the fields and didn't go down.
While the herd stood in the shallows, the drovers took their axes to the trees past the gate. They left the logs in a heap and the river running brown behind them.
{X_nameDef} said nothing at all, which was worse than arguing, and took the herd back along the dry road the way it came.
The colony stood back and let the animals run. They came through the fields in a long frightened stream, and went out the far side without stopping.
The meals went down to the gate for {FACTION}'s people on the firebreaks. {FACTION} won't forget who fed them while they dug.
Hot food went out to them, and the people from the farm ate every scrap of it standing. {X_nameDef} thanked the colony and took them on toward {PLACE} while there was still light.
The gate stays shut. {X_nameDef} asks once more through it, then turns the people from the farm back to the road.

texts.li: [winter] Two people from {PLACE} came through the snow with sacks on their backs and frost in their eyebrows. {X_nameDef} set {X_possessive} sack down at the gate first: {COUNT} {THING} between them, from {PLACE}'s own winter stores, because word had reached them the colony's were thin.

[colony:Generous] "You gave when we had nothing," says the message {X_nameDef} brought from {PLACE}, with {COUNT} {THING} on two pairs of shoulders. The colony's stores are thin, and the settlers there remember who fed them.

lines.li: The {THING} goes into the stores sack by sack. {X_nameDef} won't take anything in return, and says {PLACE} would be ashamed of {X_objective} if {X_pronoun} did.
The two from {PLACE} are sat at the colony's table before the sacks are even put away, and eat with the colony like neighbors. It's a plain meal, and they say it's the best they've had this season.
{X_nameDef} argues, and loses, and picks the sack back up. "The offer stands," {X_pronoun} says at the gate, "whenever you've stopped being proud."
